items.headline: ECI to soon launch a single-point App for stakeholders; to subsume over existing 40 IT Apps with enhanced UI/UX
items.claim: The Commission announced ECINET in May 2025 as one platform to replace more than 40 of its apps and websites for voters and election officials.
items.quote: The new one-stop platform, ECINET, will integrate and reorient over 40 of ECI’s existing mobile and web applications. ... To ensure that data is as accurate as possible, the data on ECINET will be entered solely by the authorized ECI official.

items.headline: ECINET Digital Platform launched at IICDEM-2026
items.claim: The Commission launched ECINET formally on 22 January 2026 and said its trial version had already been used during the Bihar election and the SIR.
items.quote: The beta version was successfully piloted during the 2025 Bihar Assembly Elections and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), enabling the Election Commission to deliver enhanced citizen-centric electoral services and make available all election-related information at the click of a button.

items.headline: BLO App underwent 30 changes in two months in Tamil Nadu
items.claim: The New Indian Express reported that the Android version of the booth officers' app was updated 31 times between 13 November 2025 and 20 January 2026, with no user manual for the updates, and that officials relied on the app to learn what the revision allowed.
items.quote: TNIE’s analysis of iOS and Android version logs showed that the Android version underwent 31 updates between November 13 (version 8.65) and January 20 (9.10), which is at an average of a new version released every second day. ... “The options available on the BLO App informed us what is permitted and what is not rather than detailed instructions or training material regarding the process or the use of the app,” a district-level official said.

items.headline: BLO App underwent 30 changes in two months in Tamil Nadu
items.claim: The same report quoted a Chennai booth officer who said the app often froze on her phone, so that data was lost or finished work had to be done again.
items.quote: A BLO from Chennai told TNIE that her phone couldn’t handle the application and frequently froze, leading to loss of data or redoing of completed work.

items.headline: MP Special Intensive Revision: 100 Forms A Day, BLOs Complain Of Impossible Targets; Voters Can’t Find Old Records
items.claim: Booth officers in Bhopal told the Free Press Journal they were asked to upload 100 forms a day and could not, because the booth officers' app server was down or very slow.
items.quote: They are being asked to collect and upload 100 forms a day. It is an impossible target to achieve, they say, adding that they are unable to feed the data of voters as the server of BLO App is either down or very slow.

items.headline: SIR: ECINET Portal Faces Peak-Hour Glitches
items.claim: Deccan Chronicle reported that people filling in enumeration forms on ECINET in Telangana kept being sent back to the home page, and an official put it down to the load from voters in more than a dozen states at once.
items.quote: Officials admitted the portal was hit by server overload as voters from over a dozen states under Phase 3 of SIR accessed it simultaneously. “It is a fact that people are facing issues. In Telangana, there is no need to panic as the ECI has extended the deadline till August 3,” a senior official told Deccan Chronicle.

items.headline: How ECI Tailored the Voter Registration in West Bengal “As it Deemed Fit”
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that in West Bengal the logical discrepancy check flagged five kinds of mismatch, from spelling differences between the Bengali 2002 roll and the English draft to age gaps with parents and grandparents.
items.quote: The discrepancies were of five kinds, as per ECI’s new algorithm: Differences in spelling between the names in the 2002 in Bengali script and in the 2025 draft voter rolls in English More than six voters had linked themselves to a single ancestor from the 2003 list; The age gap between a voter and their parent fell outside the 15-to-45-year range; A cited grandparent was less than 40 years older than the voter; The gender of the voter did not align with the name provided.
items.response: The Collective said it sent detailed questions to the Commission and had no answer by publication.

items.headline: How ECI Tailored the Voter Registration in West Bengal “As it Deemed Fit”
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that a registration officer showed its reporter that the button to clear voters with a name mismatch had disappeared from ERONET overnight, so such cases now needed the district officer's approval.
items.quote: “These options keep changing every other day,” the ERO told me. “Till this morning, for logical discrepancies with name mismatch, ERONET was allowing me to verify the elector by myself. Now, when I open ERONET, that button has disappeared. Now, these have to be approved by the DEO.”
items.response: The Collective said it sent detailed questions to the Commission and had no answer by publication.

items.headline: How ECI Tailored the Voter Registration in West Bengal “As it Deemed Fit”
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that district magistrates of at least three West Bengal districts wrote to the state election office asking for a written procedure for logical discrepancy cases, and that the portal accepted only the 12 listed documents.
items.quote: “Regarding logical discrepancies for mapped cases: An SOP may kindly be provided of logical discrepancy cases…and the role of BLO, ERO/AERO and DEO. Also, instruction may be provided about requisite documents to be taken at the time of hearing by ERO/AERO for such cases. It may be kindly noted that there is no provision for uploading other than 12 categories at the portal at the moment,” said the letter to the CEO.
items.response: The Collective reported that the officers received no response and carried on with their own methods.

items.headline: How ECI Tailored the Voter Registration in West Bengal “As it Deemed Fit”
items.claim: A registration officer told The Reporters' Collective that officers were told orally to ask unmapped electors for a second document besides Aadhaar, and that the software for a time would not accept Aadhaar alone. The Collective said it could not check this claim.
items.quote: “While this contradicts the original SIR instructions, we received no written orders. Just the software stopped allowing us (EROs) to only upload Aadhar. We were required by design to upload additional documents. The feature seemed to have disappeared now,” he said while showing us the interface. The Collective could not independently verify this claim.

items.headline: Verified: ECI’s top West Bengal officer sent orders to state officials for SIR on WhatsApp
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer sent instructions on a WhatsApp group of district magistrates that brought forward the enumeration deadline and asked officers to mark voters absent before the written deadline. The Trinamool Congress had first made the allegation before the Supreme Court.
items.quote: However, instructions issued solely on WhatsApp, advanced this date and asked officials to mark voters absent even before this deadline elapsed. ... We verified the informal instructions. Two officials showed the messages
items.response: The Collective said the Commission and the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer did not reply to its questions on the WhatsApp instructions.

items.headline: Verified: ECI’s top West Bengal officer sent orders to state officials for SIR on WhatsApp
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that on 29 December 2025 the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer's office told state officials in writing that the logical discrepancy software was faulty because the 2002 roll had not been digitised accurately.
items.quote: On December 29, after the enumeration phase was complete, the CEO West Bengal’s office admitted on record to state officials that the software finding ‘logical discrepancies’ was malfunctioning. This was because the base data, the 2002 voter list, had not been digitised accurately, the CEO admitted.
items.response: The Collective said the Commission and the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer did not reply to its questions.

items.headline: Order of 19.01.2026, W.P.(C) 1089/2025
items.claim: The Supreme Court recorded, from the documents before it, what the logical discrepancy category in West Bengal covered and that about 1.36 crore voters fell in it.
items.quote: The documents brought on record by the parties indicate that, within the category of logical discrepancies include, inter alia, a mismatch of the father’s name, a mismatch of parents’ ages, a difference in parents’ ages of more than 50 years, a difference in grandparents’ ages of less than 40 years, and those having more than six progeny.

items.outlet: Siasat (citing officials of the CEO West Bengal)
items.headline: West Bengal SIR: ECI explains why ‘logical discrepancy’ cases are high
items.claim: Officials of West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer said the logical discrepancy check caught people who had falsely linked themselves to unrelated voters, and gave examples found at hearings.
items.quote: “There have been cases where eight to ten voters were shown as sons or daughters of a single senior citizen voter during progeny mapping. However, during hearings, it was found that the senior citizen had only two children and had no blood relationship with most of those listed as his sons or daughters,” said an official from the CEO’s office.

items.headline: Press note No.EL.63/2026/50: CEO Meghalaya Reviews Notice and Hearing Phase of SIR 2026
items.claim: Meghalaya's Chief Electoral Officer listed six checks that ECINET used to flag mapping discrepancies in the third phase, among them a sibling age gap under nine months.
items.quote: The discrepancies identified through ECINET are: mismatch between the elector's name and the name available in the SIR 2005 records; mismatch between the elector's parent's name and the corresponding name recorded in SIR 2005; age difference between the elector and parent being less than 15 years or more than 50 years; age gap of less than nine months between siblings linked to the same parent; more than six children being linked to the same parent; and age difference of less than 40 years between an elector and grandparent.

items.headline: SIR: EC state poll machinery to share details of 'suspected foreigners' with authorities
items.claim: PTI reported that the Commission's written instructions of 14 May 2026 for the third phase told registration officers to refer suspected foreign nationals to the authority under the Citizenship Act.
items.quote: In a detailed set of instructions circulated on May 14 to state chief electoral officers on procedure to be followed while holding SIR, the poll authority said "... Also, electoral registration officers (EROs) will refer cases of suspected foreign nationals to the competent authority under the Citizenship Act, 1955. For these purposes, assistant EROs shall exercise ERO's powers independently..."

items.headline: EC explains new ERONET options for SIR notice disposal to EROs through demo video; no written instructions yet
items.claim: A Delhi registration officer told The Hindu that officers were first told to identify suspected foreigners during enumeration and later told in the middle of it to stop, and that many oral instructions had been taken back.
items.quote: “Since SIR was announced, we have received a lot of instructions, some written and some oral. Many have since been taken back. For instance, we were told to identify ‘suspected foreigners’ along with Absent, Shifted, Dead and Duplicate, and then, in the middle of the enumeration phase in Delhi, we were told not to identify or report such cases.”
items.response: The Delhi CEO’s office and the EC did not respond to The Hindu's queries.

items.headline: EC explains new ERONET options for SIR notice disposal to EROs through demo video; no written instructions yet
items.claim: The Hindu reported that new ERONET options letting registration officers clear notice cases without a hearing or documents were explained only through an eight-minute video from the Commission's IT department, with no written instruction.
items.quote: Days after adding new options to its ERONET portal that allow Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to dispose of notice cases without hearings or documents, the Election Commission (EC) is now explaining the changes to officials through a demonstration video prepared by the Election Commission’s Information Technology (IT) Department, with no written documents circulated so far, sources told The Hindu.
items.response: The Delhi CEO’s office and the EC did not respond to queries on why the options were introduced at this stage.

items.headline: EC explains new ERONET options for SIR notice disposal to EROs through demo video; no written instructions yet
items.claim: The Hindu reported that the options reached Delhi officers on 30 September and only the ten states and union territories still in the notice phase, and that a case marked ineligible still could not be reversed.
items.quote: EROs in Delhi could access the options from September 30, while the eight-minute video explaining the changes was shown to them at a meeting on Saturday (October 3, 2026). ... While the new options let EROs clear notice cases faster, including those where documents are unavailable, based on their satisfaction, they still cannot reverse a case once an elector has been marked ineligible, officials said.
items.response: The Delhi CEO’s office and the EC did not respond to queries on why the options were introduced at this stage.

items.headline: Delhi SIR: Over 350 names already marked ineligible; CEO warns against deletion on flimsy grounds
items.claim: The Hindu reported that more than 350 Delhi electors had been marked ineligible within a month of hearings, about 200 of them in Vikaspuri, and officials said the marking could not be rolled back by the registration officer or the state's Chief Electoral Officer.
items.quote: Of the 350 electors already marked ineligible less than a month into the hearings process, about 200 are from the Vikaspuri constituency; once a voter is marked ineligible, this cannot be rolled back at the level of ERO or State CEO, officials said
items.response: The Delhi Chief Electoral Officer wrote to officers on 25 September 2026 setting a 10-point checklist before marking anyone ineligible and telling them not to delete names on flimsy or frivolous grounds.

items.headline: Dozen Bengal tribunal judges flag EC portal: ‘Can’t restore deleted voters’
items.claim: The Indian Express reported that at a meeting on 11 August 2026 more than a dozen West Bengal appeal tribunal judges recorded that the Commission's portal did not let them serve notices, hold virtual hearings, restore a deleted voter or give appellants a copy of the order.
items.quote: “There is no mechanism to hold virtual hearings in case the Tribunal intends to hear the parties…Once the appeal is disposed of either by way of deletion or inclusion of the voter, it cannot be restored on the portal if the restoration is needed on account of direction of the judicial order or otherwise.”
items.response: The paper said it emailed the Commission and the Registrar General of the Calcutta High Court on 1 October and received no response.

items.headline: Maharashtra Poll Chief Seeks More ERO Powers As ECINet Faces Scrutiny Over SIR
items.claim: Outlook, citing NDTV, reported that Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer S Chockalingam asked for four changes to the ECINET software and more discretion for registration officers in logical discrepancy cases.
items.quote: Chockalingam has also sought four changes in the ECINet software, including for cases marked as “logical discrepancies”.
items.response: The Commission said on 26 September that several portal upgrades had already been made on inputs from state Chief Electoral Officers and that further flexibility needed by field officers would be made operational.

items.headline: ECINET flaws were flagged to poll body, cyber-security agency CERT-In in July: Researcher
items.claim: Hindustan Times reported that security researcher Nisarga Adhikary emailed CERT-In on 8 July 2026, copied to the Commission's complaints address, about flaws in the voter-services website and the ECINET app. The worst, in his account, let anyone obtain election officials' names and mobile numbers without logging in.
items.quote: The issue Adhikary rated as critical concerns a server behind the voter portal. He says it returned the names and mobile numbers of election officials to requests that carried no login, CAPTCHA or visible limit on the number of requests.
items.response: HT said neither CERT-In nor the Commission answered its questions of 5 October. On 6 October CERT-In told Adhikary that one flaw, the hardcoded encryption key he rated least serious, had been fixed and that work on the rest was under progress. HT said none of the flaws related directly to registration officers' access to the roll, and that the email alleged no theft or misuse of data.

items.headline: ECINET designed to centralise voter deletions from BJP headquarters, Congress alleges
items.claim: Congress alleged after the Hindustan Times report that ECINET was designed to centralise deletions and additions from the BJP's headquarters. This is a party's allegation, and the report it followed did not link the security flaws to it.
items.quote: The Congress on Thursday alleged that the Election Commission’s online portal for voter registration and related services was designed to “centralise all deletions and additions from the Bharatiya Janata Party headquarters”.
items.response: Scroll did not report a response from the Commission to this allegation.

items.headline: Cong accuses EC of 'lying' about ECINet, calls for accountability
items.claim: Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh alleged that by restricting registration officers' access to the ECINet roll system and overruling them in Goa, West Bengal and other states, the Commission broke the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
items.quote: “By restricting access of Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to the ECINet voter roll system and by overruling EROs in states like Goa, West Bengal and others, the ECI controlled by the CEC has violated The Representation of the People Act, 1950 and the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960,” Ramesh said.
items.response: PTI reported that the Commission has said differing views are a normal part of deliberation and that all its orders carry full legal sanction and follow established statutory procedures.

items.headline: ECINet is decentralised, only designated officials have access, says ECI
items.claim: Commission officials said ECINET is decentralised, that each field officer acts through their own login, and that nobody at headquarters can perform those officers' statutory functions. ERONET is now part of ECINET.
items.quote: “No one else can perform their statutory function on ECINet, including any other officer of the ECI,” an official said. Cybersecurity for the platform is, however, provided centrally by the ECI. ... Official documents refer to it as the “Electoral Roll module of ECINET Portal (previously ERONET)”.

items.headline: The meeting of the Commission was held today i.e. 26.09.2026 at 3:00 PM
items.claim: After its full meeting on 26 September 2026 the Commission said field officers have access to ECINET by role, set up a committee with an independent expert to check ECINET against the law, and said new IT modules would first go to a committee of officers.
items.quote: Field officers have role-based access to the ECINET system as per their statutory powers. A Committee headed by Sr. Deputy Election Commissioner (DEC) and including an independent expert from IIT/IIIT will review the ECINET to double-check that it complies with the provisions of the Acts and Rules and submit report to the Commission. ... Henceforth, all the new initiatives about IT modules and portals will be discussed in the Committee of Officers (COO) before approval by the Commission.

items.headline: 'Misleading': ECI fact-checks Rahul Gandhi's Form 6 claim, cites SC ruling on Bihar SIR order
items.claim: Rahul Gandhi of the Congress, the Leader of the Opposition, said the Chief Election Commissioner had changed Form 6 illegally and unilaterally. The Commission replied on X that the statement was misleading, that its Bihar order of 24 June 2025 had the Commission's unanimous approval and was upheld by the Supreme Court on 27 May 2026, and that its press note of 26 September said the declaration attached to Form 6 had been upheld, Business Today reported.
items.quote: "It is now established beyond doubt that Gyanesh Kumar changed Form 6 illegally and unilaterally," Gandhi said. ... Fact Check ❌The statement made in this post is misleading ✅1) The order for SIR in Bihar issued on 24 June 2025 was issued with the unanimous approval of the Commission. This order has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its judgment dated 27 May 2026 ✅2) In its Press Note No. 120 dated 26 September 2026, in Point 1(iii), ECI has stated that, "The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court." #ECIFactCheck— Election Commission of India (@ECISVEEP) October 5, 2026
items.note: The same Business Today report says the Supreme Court said that day it had not approved any modification to Form 6 (see court-31).

items.headline: Goa CEO says 88 of 97 voters left out after SIR have filed Form 6, applications accepted
items.claim: Goa's Chief Electoral Officer said on X that 88 of the 97 voters missing from the final roll of February 2026 had filed Form 6 and been accepted, The Pioneer reported. The cases came to light after The Indian Express reported that the Commission's software did not let verified electors be added.
items.quote: The Goa CEO's office on Thursday released the status of all 97 cases, saying 88 voters had submitted Form 6 and their applications had been accepted.
items.note: ThePrint's PTI copy (2 Oct 2026, 09:45 IST) is behind a bot check, so the quote is from The Pioneer's version '(with inputs from PTI)'; a summary of ThePrint's page agreed on every figure. The Wire (court-32's source) dates the CEO's X post to Thursday 1 October. The CEO's X post itself was not opened.

items.headline: 'Dead' on voter list, but alive: 3 Vijayapura women demand action over SIR controversy
items.claim: The Week reported that eight of 1,054 voters on a deletion list submitted by Vijayapura City MLA Basanagouda Patil Yatnal were shown as dead on death certificates, and three living women among them demanded action.
items.quote: "Instead, the inquiry into Yatnal's complaint was opened under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act."
items.response: Deputy Commissioner and District Electoral Officer Anandh K said officials were still seeking legal opinion on how to proceed. No response from the MLA was reported.
items.note: The three women are named on the page and are not named here. 'Allegedly fabricated' is the page's wording about the certificates.

items.headline: 'Was Ghosted': Why [the researcher] Wrote to Election Commission and CERT-in in July
items.claim: The security researcher who reported the ECINET flaws told The Wire that the Commission and CERT-In did not answer him until Hindustan Times asked, and that the issue CERT-In said was resolved was the most minor.
items.quote: According to him, it was the most minor of the lot.
items.response: No statement from the Commission was reported.
items.note: Follow-up to soft-23 (Hindustan Times, 8 October). The researcher is a private person and is named by role.

items.headline: The ECI Software Deleted 5.38 Lakh Bengal Voters With Auto-Generated Rejections Without Citing a Reason
items.claim: The Wire reported that 5,38,320 names were deleted from West Bengal's roll between the draft of December 2025 and the final roll of 28 February 2026 through Form 7s that the Commission's software generated in the officer's name when an officer did not approve an elector at a hearing. In the Form 10 registers it read for 284 of the 294 constituencies, 5,23,998 deletions give the Electoral Registration Officer as the objector and leave the reason blank, and 422 give an individual objector. The Chief Electoral Officer's statement of 6 March 2026 said the state's Form 7 figure included these auto-generated forms.
items.quote: The figure of deletion due to Form 7 as mentioned, includes the auto generated Form 7 generated due to rejection of Enumeration Forms (EFs) as electors not found eligible for Final Roll. This Figure which was received from ECI (Election Commission of India) by mail on 28.02.26 in 5,38,320 (sic).
items.response: The Wire reported that the Additional Chief Electoral Officer of West Bengal told it Form 10 gives no option to record details, and that those deleted can apply again through Form 6.
items.note: By Aparna Bhattacharya, published 17 October 2026, 8:00 am IST, read in full with curl on 19 October 2026. The quote is the Chief Electoral Officer's statement of 6 March 2026 on X as The Wire prints it; the post itself was not opened. Same mechanism as the Uttar Pradesh items in up.json (The Reporters' Collective, 9 October). Figures to check: the article dates the draft 14 December 2025, and also says 'Only 7,733 of the Form 7 rejections because a person actually filed the form', which does not agree with its own count of 422 individual objectors in 284 seats; it later writes 5.46 lakh for the same Form 7 total. The 10 seats not read (eight in Cooch Behar, two in Alipurduar) hold 14,061 more Form 7 deletions. The article also counts seats where these deletions exceed the 2026 margin (six of 283) and guesses religion from names; neither is carried here. 'Struck off' and 'removed' are the outlet's words. The Additional CEO is named in the article and is given here by office.

items.headline: Audit finds Bengal-specific access curbs in ECINET code
items.claim: The Hindustan Times reported a review of ECINET's publicly served code by the civic-tech initiative Charchagram, which found a rule written into the code that excludes Electoral Registration Officers and Assistant Electoral Registration Officers in West Bengal, and in no other state, from the View Enumeration Form Details page and the notice-and-hearing dashboard of the SIR Phase II landing page. The enumeration form page lists each form with its documents and the booth level officer's recommendation, and holds the hearing orders. The review read only the code a browser receives before login, on 2, 6, 7 and 9 October and in a build fetched on 19 October, so it cannot say whether the rule was ever applied, whether the server enforces it, or when it was added. The paper could not verify the review independently.
items.quote: West Bengal is separately hard-coded in the codebase and excluded from it (for ERO and AERO).
items.response: The Hindustan Times reported that the Election Commission did not answer a questionnaire it sent.
items.note: By Himanshi Dahiya, published 20 October 2026, 7:15 am IST (datePublished 2026-10-20T07:15:03+05:30), read in full from the page's articleBody with curl on 20 October 2026. The quote is the reviewer's, as the paper prints it; he is a data scientist at Charchagram and is given here by role. Other quotations in the article: 'We reviewed only the front-end JavaScript bundle that the site serves publicly ... We called no endpoints and used no login or credentials at any point'; 'Server-side enforcement isn't visible to us'; on earlier builds, 'We don't know.' The paper says the current build was introduced on 16 October and the reviewer first saw the rule on 28 September. The article also carries Abhishek Banerjee's allegation of 21 February that EROs in Bengal could no longer monitor AEROs on ECINET (RPA ss.13B and 13C), and a Supreme Court advocate's view that such a rule, if applied, would run against the Court's order of 24 February making EROs and AEROs responsible for satisfying the judicial officers; the advocate is given by role. The article's own figures for West Bengal (27.1 lakh disenfranchised, 7.8% at the draft, 1.36 crore flagged, 22 lakh removed after adjudication, 10% at the final) are the paper's and are not carried here; the site's West Bengal figures come from the CEO's PN-05-2026. Also syndicated by IPA Newspack the same day.

items.headline: On ECINet platform, access for States can be switched off and on centrally: report
items.claim: The Hindu reported a second finding from Saurav Rajput's review of ECINET's code for the civic-tech initiative Charchagram. Behind the official login the portal has an area for managing State Nodal Officers, and each officer's row has a disable button whose confirmation says the user will no longer be able to access the application. Separately, the code carries the message that viewing enumeration form details is not enabled for the selected State, which the review reads as a feature switched on or off State by State. The review read only code the site serves before login. The paper says it was not clear since when the feature has been on the portal, which was launched in January 2026, and the reviewer said he had seen it since 28 September.
items.quote: On disabling this State Nodal Officer, the user will no longer be able to access the application.
items.response: The Hindu carried a statement by the Congress general secretary (communications), Jairam Ramesh, that the ECINET system and the Commission's IT division had overruled the statutory authority of Electoral Registration Officers. It reported no response from the Commission.
items.note: By Sreeparna Chakrabarty, published 20 October 2026, 9:55 pm IST (datePublished 2026-10-20T21:55:57+05:30), read with curl on 21 October 2026 from the page's articleBody; the page marks it as not free to read. The quote is the pop-up text as the paper prints it. The paper itself goes further than the code it describes: it says the State-by-State message 'in turn means that access for State Nodal Officers (SNOs) can be switched off', which joins two separate things, a disable button on each officer's account and a per-State switch on one screen. The claim keeps them apart. Nothing in the report says who can press the button or the switch, or that either was used. A post on X of 20 October relaying the report adds that the switch 'sits in Delhi' and that officers in West Bengal 'are blocked'; neither is in the report, and the West Bengal finding is soft-33's, which says only that the code can bar them. Charchagram's own site links the report and carries no report of its own. The paper describes the reviewer as an alumnus of IIT Delhi and IIM Calcutta; he is named on the owner's decision of 20 October 2026, as in soft-33.

items.headline: ECINET Audit Finds State-Level Access Could be Restricted by Election Commission, VIP Tags for Voters
items.claim: The Wire reported three findings from Saurav Rajput's review of ECINET's code for the civic-tech initiative Charchagram, made on 2, 6, 7 and 9 October from code the site serves publicly, with no passwords and no use of ECINET's programming interfaces. Besides the State Nodal Officer controls and the West Bengal rule in the two reports before it, the review found code showing that the officials' portal marks some voters with a gold VIP symbol on the screen that shows the documents in an enumeration form, and a button that downloads a list of these VIP electors by Assembly constituency, which can be narrowed by state, district, constituency and polling part. The criteria for marking a voter are not known. The review cannot say whether any of these features were used, by whom or how often. The Reporters' Collective earlier reported a Mark VIP module in the booth level officers' app, and Charchagram says its review examined the other end of that chain.
items.quote: At present, we cannot say whether these features have been used, or prove how they have been used
items.response: The report carries no response from the Commission.
items.note: By Pragya Singh, published 21 October 2026, 7:09 pm IST (AMP datePublished 2026-10-21T19:09:29+05:30; the desktop page's JSON-LD writes the same moment as 13:39:29 with a +05:30 offset), read in full from the articleBody on 22 October 2026. The quote is the reviewer's, as the paper prints it. The report also quotes him calling the publicly served code 'very, very bad quality coding' and says Charchagram has filed applications under the RTI Act. Charchagram's own site links this report and carries no audit document of its own (checked 22 October 2026). The Reporters' Collective's report on the Mark VIP module is on the reading list.

items.headline: TMC seeks EC explanation on Bengal specific feature in voter’s enumeration forms in ECINET
items.claim: Millennium Post reported that the Trinamool Congress, reacting to the Hindustan Times report of the same day on the West Bengal rule in ECINET's code, asked the Election Commission who had authorised the Bengal-specific changes, why West Bengal was treated differently from other states, who is accountable and what safeguards protect every eligible voter's rights. The party also asked when the Chief Election Commissioner would take responsibility and resign.
items.quote: Who authorised these Bengal-specific changes, and Why?
items.response: The report carries no response from the Commission.
items.note: By Mpost Bureau, published 20 October 2026, 11:37 pm IST (article:published_time 2026-10-20T23:37:25+05:30), read in full on 22 October 2026. The quote is the party's statement as the paper prints it. The report repeats figures from the Hindustan Times report for West Bengal (2.71 million, and about 3.8 million appeals before the tribunals) in its own words; they are not carried here, and the site's West Bengal figures come from the CEO's PN-05-2026. Charchagram's site links this report.

items.headline: Maharashtra CEO Seeks Changes to Form 6
items.claim: Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer wrote to the Commission asking it to change Form 6 so that electors left off the draft in the revision can register again without declaring themselves first-time voters, Deccan Chronicle reported. The letter says officers find it hard to persuade such electors to sign a form that carries a penalty for a false declaration. It asks for the words "new voters" to be taken out of the form's title, for a separate declaration for people who were enrolled before and are no longer on any roll, and for a place to give the earlier EPIC number.
items.quote: Election officials have reported difficulties in persuading such voters to submit Form 6, as many fear that declaring themselves first-time applicants despite having been registered previously could expose them to legal action.
items.response: Officials said that any change to the statutory Form 6 would need the Central government to amend the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. No decision by the Commission was reported.
items.note: Deccan Chronicle (DC Correspondent, Mumbai), published 18 October 2026, 11:58 pm IST, read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 24 October 2026; the AMP and desktop pages carry the same text. The paper says the letter was sent last week and does not quote it, so the date is the publication date. The quote is the paper's own sentence. The Indian Express original and The Quint's report of it were not read. Related: court-48, the Supreme Court application on the same declaration in Delhi.

items.headline: Details of software used in SIR exempt from RTI, Election Commission cites 'trade secrets'
items.claim: In a reply dated 16 October to an RTI application from a social activist in Karimnagar, the Commission declined to give the name and version of the software it used to find errors and anomalies in the rolls during the revision, citing commercial confidence, trade secrets and intellectual property under Section 8(1)(d), the Hindustan Times reported. It called the questions on automatic flagging, artificial intelligence and safeguards against wrongful flagging a clarification outside the definition of information, and cited Section 8(1)(g) on who reviews flagged records.
items.quote: no new software has been developed or procured for the SIR exercise
items.response: The Commission said Electoral Registration Officers decide on including or excluding an elector on the basis of facts and records, and that under Sections 13B(1) and 13B(2) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 the officer of each constituency prepares and revises its roll.
items.note: Himanshi Dahiya in the Hindustan Times, 25 October 2026, 6:35 am IST, read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 25 October 2026. The applicant is named in the report and given here by role. The reply is also on the RTI page as rti-19. Related: rti-08, the reply of 21 July on the West Bengal module, which cited the same section.

items.headline: UP MLC Voter List: 'राम ने शर्मा को मारा', पिता का नाम- 'टक्कर मारना'; वोटर लिस्ट में अजीबोगरीब नाम
items.claim: Voter slips for the Legislative Council election in the Allahabad-Jhansi graduates' constituency, where polling was set for 23 October, carried Hindi phrases in place of electors' and fathers' names, and pictures of them spread on social media before the polling parties left, Dainik Jagran reported. On the instructions of the Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, the Returning Officer, Bimal Kumar Dubey, who is Divisional Commissioner of Jhansi, had the roll checked and reported clerical errors and more than 100 duplicate names. The Bharatiya Janata Party separately complained to the Chief Electoral Officer that the roll held 4,397 duplicate electors, and that electors born between 2001 and 2005 were on it whom the party called too young to qualify. The party's Prayagraj city president put 3,163 of the duplicates in Prayagraj.
items.quote: जांच में मतदाता सूची में लिपकीय त्रुटियों के साथ ही 100 से अधिक डुप्लीकेट मतदाताओं के नाम भी सामने आए हैं।
items.response: The Returning Officer said in a press note of 17 October that no elector would be denied the vote because of a clerical error, and that an elector whose identity satisfied the presiding officer or polling officer would be allowed to vote. The report says the clerical errors found in the check were marked and corrected, and that a separate list of the duplicate names was being given to the presiding officers of the polling stations concerned, with instructions to keep a special watch on those names during the poll. The Indian Express reported on 26 October that the office of the Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, replied on X to the Aam Aadmi Party's Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh, who had asked the Chief Election Commissioner why a voter slip read “Ram ne Yadav ko Maara” and whether the Commission's computer was casteist. The reply said the roll of the recent Legislative Council election also carried the entry “Ram ne Sharma ko Maara”, and the office shared a slip from the graduates' constituency election with that phrase in place of an elector's father's name. The paper quotes Rinwa as saying “Computers/software are not casteist” and “We accept that an error was made, but fortunately, even while making the error, no caste discrimination took place. Thank God that Ram did not hit a minority. Otherwise, besides being accused of casteism, we would have also faced allegations of communalism.”
items.note: Dainik Jagran (Jagran Correspondent, Jhansi), 22 October 2026, 3:30 pm IST, and its report from Prayagraj of the same day, 2:14 pm IST, both read in full with curl on 25 October 2026. This roll is the graduates' constituency roll for the Legislative Council. The Election Commission's letter No. 322/1.C/G&T/E-ROLL/2026-BIEN of 12 September 2025 ordered it prepared afresh under Rule 31 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, on applications in Form 18, with 1 November 2025 as the qualifying date. It is a separate roll from the Assembly roll revised in the SIR. The reports call the errors clerical and do not say how the phrases came to be entered. A post on X circulating the slips attributes them to the Commission's software translating names, and neither report says so. The district figures given by the party's Prayagraj city president add up to 4,397. No elector is named here. The Chief Electoral Officer's reply is from The Indian Express (Express Web Desk, with inputs from PTI), 'Thank God Ram didn't hit a minority': UP CEO office's jibe in voter slip row, https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/lucknow/up-ceo-navdeep-rinwa-aap-sanjay-singh-voter-slip-error-ram-yadav-casteism-row-10937083/, datePublished 2026-10-26T13:30:07+05:30, read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 26 October 2026. The report gives the reply in English and does not say what language the post was written in, and the post itself was not opened. The report names the elector on the shared slip and the elector whose name Sanjay Singh's slip rendered as a phrase, and neither is given here. It does not say which roll Sanjay Singh's slip came from, and it says nothing about how the entries were made beyond the reply's words on computers and software.

items.headline: Pending SIR notice lists published for only 39 assembly constituencies out of 288 so far
items.claim: Lists of electors whose notices were still pending had been published for 39 of Maharashtra's 288 Assembly constituencies, in 14 districts, on the election authorities' websites by Saturday 24 October, The Times of India reported. Officials said the lists hold only unresolved cases and do not cover all 1.22 crore notices generated in the revision. In Pune district only the Shivajinagar list was up, with one elector on it, and in Mumbai the lists for Malabar Hill, Byculla, Dharavi, Dahisar and Vandre West. A circular of 23 October from the Chief Electoral Officer's office told electoral registration officers to download the data from the Commission's ECINET platform, compile one PDF for each constituency, publish it on the district election officer's website by 26 October and share part-wise lists with parties' booth level agents. Officials said documents some electors had given booth level officers during enumeration were not uploaded because the system did not support it then. Notices are to be disposed of by 10 November and the final roll is due on 16 November.
items.quote: The lists cover voters whose names could not be matched with previous electoral rolls, categorised as ‘No Mapping’, and those whose records showed logical discrepancies despite successful mapping. A name appearing on the list does not mean the voter has been finally deleted from the electoral roll,
items.response: An electoral official said a name on the list does not mean the elector has been finally deleted from the roll, and the report says the Chief Electoral Officer's office will review whether district election authorities have complied with the circular.
items.note: Nisha Nambiar in The Times of India, Pune, datePublished 2026-10-25T01:00:00+05:30, read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 26 October 2026. The quote is an unnamed electoral official's, as the paper prints it. The report's inset also gives Form 6, 7 and 8 totals for Maharashtra (10.94 lakh, 50,800 and 5.5 lakh) from a source in the Chief Electoral Officer's office, with 26 October as the last day to file them; they are not carried here. Placed under software because the circular routes the lists through ECINET and the report ties the missing documents to what the system could take at enumeration. The draft roll was published on 31 August.

items.headline: Judges of Bengal tribunals ask Election Commission to fix portal, drop Aadhaar authentication
items.claim: The appellate tribunals of retired High Court judges that hear appeals in West Bengal's revision have asked the Election Commission at least twice in four weeks to remove an Aadhaar authentication step from its portal, because without it they cannot upload final orders, The Indian Express reported from official records. The screen was added on 21 September, the judges asked in writing on 24 September for it to be removed, and on 13 October the tribunals told the Chief Electoral Officer's office again that the system did not let them upload final orders. Orders are being disposed of on paper and not uploaded. The portal also limits the documents the judges can accept to the 13 the Commission listed for the revision. On 1 October ten of the judges wrote about their working conditions at Joka, about 30 km from Kolkata and New Town, and asked for the tribunals to be moved to a more central place and for an honorarium befitting the judges. They noted that a request to raise it from Rs 25,000 a week to Rs 50,000 had been pending with the Chief Justice since June. The report says the Commission told the Supreme Court that 38.31 lakh appeals had been filed as of 18 September, 22.21 lakh by deleted electors and 16.10 lakh against inclusions, and that 1.26 lakh had been disposed of by 10 September.
items.quote: The Honourable Judges at the Appellate Tribunal require the Aadhaar authentication screen removed from the AT portal for the purpose of disposal of appeals.
items.response: The Election Commission did not respond to the paper's queries mailed to its spokesperson on 21 October.
items.note: Damini Nath in The Indian Express, New Delhi, published 27 October 2026 at 5:55 am IST, read in full with Firecrawl on 28 October 2026. The quote is from the letter of 24 September by the tribunals' venue-in-charge to the Additional Chief Electoral Officer and nodal officer for tribunals, as the paper prints it. The paper first reported the portal's gaps on 7 October, from the minutes of the judges' meeting of 11 August. Placed under software because the dispute is about what the Commission's portal lets the tribunals do.

items.headline: Did 27 Lakhs Lose the Right to Vote Because the EC Software Switched Bengal Voters Already Decided by EROs Over to Judges Overnight?
items.claim: Electoral registration officers in Murshidabad had decided almost every hearing case before them by the deadline of 21 February, and a week later far more electors were marked under adjudication and sent to judicial officers than the officers had left pending, The Wire reported from the Commission's ERONET status reports. At 10 pm on 21 February, of 18,84,772 electors called for hearings in the district's 22 constituencies, the officers had parked 18,30,045 for the final roll, found 41,214 ineligible and left 13,513 pending. On 28 February 11,01,145 Murshidabad electors were under adjudication, and judicial officers deleted 4,55,137 of them. In Samserganj 2,391 cases were pending on deadline night, 1,08,400 electors went to adjudication and 74,775 were deleted. Nadia's report of 4:04 am on 22 February shows 57,525 pending, and The Wire puts 2,67,940 of the district's electors under adjudication. An assistant electoral registration officer told The Wire that after hearings closed on 14 February the portal stopped taking document uploads and gained a category, Documents to be reviewed, into which micro-observers and roll observers moved electors the officers had parked for the final roll, and that those the officers then approved again went to adjudication. On 20 February Congress MP Isha Khan Choudhury wrote to the Chief Electoral Officer that the Malda District Magistrate had told an all-party meeting that 5.91 lakh cases had been returned for review that day. Subrata Gupta, the Commission's special roll observer, told The Wire that the observers had recommended a review of lakhs of cases the officers had cleared and that the decisions had to be taken by the registration officers.
items.quote: Of 18,84,772 voters called for hearings across the district’s 22 constituencies, they had approved 18,30,045 for the final rolls and found 41,214 ineligible. Only 13,513 cases were still pending.
items.response: On 1 March the Chief Electoral Officer's office posted on X that names were marked under adjudication because the registration officers had not decided them after hearing. On 2 March it posted that it had nowhere said all such cases were due to indecision by the officers, and that a certain number had remained pending and were referred for adjudication. Gupta said the Commission had told the observers that about 60 lakh of about 1.5 crore cases heard were pending and were referred to judicial officers, and that he could not say whether these were the cases marked for review. The Wire says it has written to the Commission and to the current and previous Chief Electoral Officers, and no reply is reported.
items.note: By Aparna Bhattacharya in The Wire, published 30 October 2026 at 11:00 am IST (post_date_gmt 05:30:05), read in full through The Wire's CMS API (posts/detail) on 30 October 2026, with the images opened. The Murshidabad status report, headed 'Report Regarding Hearing & Document Verification 21/02/2026 @ 10 pm', gives the totals 18,84,772, 41,214, 18,30,045 (97.10%) and 13,513, and Samserganj at 1,14,712, 884, 1,11,437 and 2,391. The Nadia report, headed 'Park for Final Pending Report (Hearing Report as on 22-02-2026 04:04:16)', gives 8,03,291 notices, 1,65,642 found ineligible, 5,80,124 parked and 57,525 pending. The MP's letter of 20 February, which carries a receipt stamp, reads '5.91 lacs cases have been returned for review today'. The figures for adjudication and deletion are from what The Wire calls the SIR master list and appear in its own table, which is not a primary document. District officials shared the status reports with political parties, and they were not checked against any other source. The assistant registration officer is anonymous, and the account of the new category and the closed uploads is that officer's, The Wire adds that BLOs raised the closed uploads in a Facebook group at the time, and it cites Trinamool Congress posts on X of 18 and 21 February about observers' logins and about electoral registration officers losing access to the portal on deadline day. Not carried here: unnamed sources' account of the two Election Commissioners' concern over this step, the association leader's estimate that 18 to 19 lakh of the 27 lakh deleted were genuine, which The Wire says it could not verify, and allegations about where observers' logins were used, which it also could not verify. The report says the SIR section was taken off ERONET within a day or two of 21 February, on the officer's word. Isha Khan Choudhury is a sitting MP and is named. The Wire's minimum counts of approved electors sent to adjudication (10.46 lakh in Murshidabad) are its own subtraction and are not carried.
